questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Australia has long been a destination I aspired to study in. I chose Monash University in particular because of its outstanding actuarial program - the only one in Australia with multiple accreditations, and notably, Monash holds three.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Finding the necessary information upon arrival was very easy. The orientation days for exchange students were well structured and informative, and the friendliness and kindness of both staff and students made settling in much easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received general guidance upon arrival, but I did not seek out any further assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find off-campus housing. I recommend waiting until you arrive in Melbourne so you can view rooms in person and meet potential roommates. The app "flatmates" was particularly helpful. Other students got lucky through different facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living close to the city center is very convenient, but it can be more expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many housing options available to students. I ultimately found my own accommodation, as I preferred to live closer to the city center.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was generally straightforward, though some information - such as unit timetables - was only available a few weeks before classes began.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Timetables for different units were not accessible until a few weeks before the start of classes. However, there was flexibility to change units up until the third teaching week, which was helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistance was available both via email and in person during the orientation week.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registering for the units I initially wanted, though I later changed two units to achieve a better timetable.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t stress too much about the registration process. You can always change units after a few weeks once you have a better sense of the courses and timetable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were easier than those at UCPH, but that was likely because I had already covered much of the material earlier. The manageable workload gave me the chance to explore Australia alongside my studies. While some other Danish students felt the units were too easy and sometimes boring, I personally was quite happy with the level. I also chose courses based on interest rather than how easy they were to pass :)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style involved far more assignments and continuous assessment, rather than a single final exam counting for 100% of the grade, as is common at UCPH.

It also felt more modern, with full access to online materials and recorded lectures, and some classes being offered exclusively online.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ETC5256 (Statistical modelling for actuarial studies), ETC5342 (Applied insurance methods), ETC5521 (Diving deeply into data exploration), ETC5523 (Communicating with data).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ETC5523 (Communicating with Data):
I would highly recommend this course due to the excellent lecturer, who has a strong mathematical background and delivered some of the most entertaining lectures I’ve had. While the course is not particularly actuarial, it significantly improves communication skills and teaches how to build a Shiny app.

ETC5342 (Applied Insurance Methods):
This course covers material similar to Skade 1, StatIns, and QRM. It was interesting to see how actuarial subjects are taught in another country. However, the lecturer was less clear, as the teaching was somewhat unstructured and the heavy accent made it difficult to follow at times.

ETC5256 (Statistical modelling for actuarial studies): 
This was a relatively easy course, but the lecturer was excellent (although it was his final semester teaching at Monash). The course includes Bayesian estimation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and eating out were generally less expensive than expected, especially coffee. Alcohol (apart from wine) was more expensive. 
Travel to and from the airport was also expensive, as there is no good public transport connection

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide range of cultural, athletic, and social activities—essentially everything you could think of. Clayton Campus in particular has a strong “campus vibe,” which I really enjoyed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I’d recommend taking advantage of the free Monday dinners from the MSA. The swimming pools are also great for a relaxing break between classes. Most importantly, just join a club you find interesting - it’s an easy way to meet people and make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Weekends:
Great Ocean Road
Grampains National Park
Sightseeing around Melbourne
Surfcamp

Holidays:
Anywhere in Australia is amazing!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, as the cultural values are quite similar to those in Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don’t be afraid to start conversations - people are very friendly. Try to join or take initiative in social activities early on then it's way more fun in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Being mindful of how to correctly address and refer to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and openness of people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be mindful when choosing your units:
Among all the Danes I met at Monash (maybe 30) we were only two students that were content with the academic level. But at the same time, we were the only ones that chose units we found interesting and not because they were easy to pass.

The actuarial program is outstanding:
Monash offers an exceptional actuarial program and is the only university in Australia with three professional accreditations, making it particularly strong for actuarial students.

Take advantage of the overall exchange experience:
The workload is generally manageable, which gives you a great opportunity to explore Australia, travel, and engage in social and campus life - something that really adds to the exchange experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a long train ride to the campus - try to find some friends to do the trip with.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friendships and experiencing studying in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to do as much as possible in one semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
